title: Queen checkmate (K+Q vs K)
summary: Box the king toward an edge with the queen a knight's-move away, then bring your king up. Avoid stalemate!

title: Rook checkmate (K+R vs K)
summary: Use the rook to cut off a rank, march your king up to oppose, then deliver the ladder mate.

title: Pawn promotion with opposition
summary: Get your king in front of the pawn and take the opposition — your king leads, the pawn follows.

title: Two-rook ladder mate
summary: Drive the king up the board one rank at a time, swinging a rook to safety whenever it's attacked.

title: Hold the draw: K vs K+P with opposition
summary: Keep your king directly in front of the enemy pawn and take the opposition. Don't let the enemy king march around you — it's a draw.

title: Lucena position (R+P vs R)
summary: Build a 'bridge': bring your rook to the 4th rank to shield your king from checks as it escapes the pawn's file.

title: Two-bishop checkmate (K+B+B vs K)
summary: Two bishops mate by driving the king into a corner. Keep the bishops side by side controlling adjacent diagonals, and bring your king to help.

title: Back-rank mate pattern
summary: The enemy king is trapped behind its own pawns. Deliver mate on the back rank in one move — find it!

title: Winning K+P: king in front
summary: Your king is in front of the pawn on the 6th rank — this always wins. Use your king to clear a path and shepherd the pawn home.

title: Connected passed pawns
summary: Two connected passers beat a lone king. Advance them side by side so they defend each other — never let one be captured for free.

title: Hold the draw: wrong-bishop rook pawn
summary: The h8 promotion square is the wrong colour for this bishop, so it can never be controlled. Sit your king in the corner (Kg8–Kh8) and it's a draw.

title: Hold the draw: K vs K + rook pawn
summary: With your king in the corner the pawn promotes to, the enemy king can never make progress without stalemating you. Shuffle Kg8–Kh8.

title: Back-rank mate
summary: A king trapped behind its own pawns is mated along the back rank by a rook or queen.

steps.note: A king trapped behind its own pawns is mated along the back rank by a rook or queen.

title: Smothered mate
summary: A king hemmed in by its own pieces is mated by a knight — nothing can block a knight check.

steps.note: A king hemmed in by its own pieces is mated by a knight — nothing can block a knight check.

title: Two-rook (ladder) mate
summary: One rook cuts off a rank while the other delivers mate on the next — the staircase mate.

steps.note: One rook cuts off a rank while the other delivers mate on the next — the staircase mate.

title: Queen + king mate
summary: The queen, supported by its king, boxes the enemy king against the edge.

steps.note: The queen, supported by its king, boxes the enemy king against the edge.

title: Scholar's mate
summary: The classic four-move attack: the queen takes f7, defended by the bishop on c4.

steps.note: The classic four-move attack: the queen takes f7, defended by the bishop on c4.

title: Arabian mate
summary: Knight and rook combine to trap a king in the corner — one of the oldest known mates.

steps.note: Knight and rook combine to trap a king in the corner — one of the oldest known mates.

title: Dovetail mate
summary: The queen mates a king whose only flight squares are blocked by its own pieces.

steps.note: The queen mates a king whose only flight squares are blocked by its own pieces.

title: Queen corner mate
summary: With the king supporting from g6, the queen delivers mate on the back rank corner.

steps.note: With the king supporting from g6, the queen delivers mate on the back rank corner.

title: Epaulette mate
summary: The king's own rooks sit on its shoulders like epaulettes, blocking every escape.

steps.note: The king's own rooks sit on its shoulders like epaulettes, blocking every escape.

title: Bishop + rook mate
summary: A long-range bishop covers escape squares while the rook mates on the back rank.
